name: Confluensis
description: Quaesitorial covenant of the Normandy Tribunal, founded in 810, which moved to the Orchard of Sour Apples in 1051 and opposes the creation of a Lotharingian Tribunal.

name: Normandy Tribunal
description: The Tribunal covering northern France, renamed from the Tribunal of the West Franks in 983; it meets every seven years.

name: Rhine Tribunal
description: Neighboring Tribunal for which the pro-Lotharingian faction is a minor annoyance; home of the covenant of Fengheld.

name: Lotharingian Tribunal
description: A proposed new Tribunal whose creation would strip rich vis sources from Normandy; also one of the Tribunals named at the Sixth Grand Tribunal in 865.

name: Pro-Lotharingian Tribunal Faction
description: Faction seeking to create a new Lotharingian Tribunal from parts of the Normandy and Rhine Tribunals ahead of the Grand Tribunal of 1228.

name: Grand Tribunal
description: The Order-wide gathering of Hermes, meeting every 33 years since 832; the 17th is due in 1228.

name: Brittany
description: Region holding more vis and faerie sites than anywhere else in the Normandy Tribunal, dominated by House Tytalus; added to the Tribunal in 1018.

name: House Tytalus
description: Hermetic House dominating Brittany, whose domus magna is Fudarus; its founder Tytalus vanished in 807.

name: Vis
description: Raw magical power harvested from vis sources, whose distribution is contested in the Normandy Tribunal.

name: Quaesitor
description: Hermetic investigators and judges of House Guernicus; Confluensis is a Quaesitorial covenant.

name: Mercer House
description: A Redcap way-station; Confluensis has investigated a site for a new one in the Lotharingian region.

name: Forest of Broceliande
description: Haunted forest in Brittany where numerous covenants have been founded but none survived.

name: Fudarus
description: Covenant founded by Tytalus in 798 to train Hariste; the domus magna of House Tytalus, site of the Betrayal of 961.

name: Faerie
description: Fae beings whose sites abound in Brittany and who make mischief for covenants there.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The order of Hermetic magi, founded in 767 by Bonisagus and the Founders.

name: Order of Preachers
description: Newly formed religious order charged with combating heresy, prominent in the Albigensian Crusade.

name: Albigensian Crusade
description: Crusade against the Cathars in the Provençal Tribunal, begun 1209 and ending 1229.

name: Provençal Tribunal
description: Tribunal to the south whose border with Normandy was set on linguistic grounds in 1102.

name: Cathars
description: Heretical group fought in the Albigensian Crusade.

name: Papal Letter of Inquisition
description: Extremely rare document granting its bearer extraordinary power backed by the papacy; only one Dominican holds one.

name: Eloi of Cunfin
description: Magus of Cunfin concerned that Church inquisitors may turn northward.

name: Jerome of Confluensis
description: Magus of Confluensis concerned about the Church's inquisitors.

name: Cunfin
description: Covenant founded in 1192.

name: Knights Hospitaller
description: Order of Hospitallers that founded a City of God settlement on the Cotentin Peninsula.

name: City of God
description: Planned perfect settlement ruled by the Church, likely with a high Dominion aura; the Hospitallers founded one near Confluensis.

name: Dominion
description: The divine Realm; a City of God would have a high Dominion aura (4 for the Hospitaller settlement).

name: Aura
description: Realm-aligned supernatural area strength, e.g. a Dominion aura of 4.

name: Cotentin Peninsula
description: Norman peninsula where Confluensis lies and the Hospitallers founded their City of God.

name: True Faith
description: Virtue often borne by the Hospitaller knights.

name: Relic
description: Holy relics carried by the Hospitaller knights.

name: Demon
description: Infernal beings that may covertly aid those opposing the pious knights.

name: Djinn
description: Beings the old crusaders may have faced in battle.

name: Grog
description: Covenant soldiers and servants whom Hospitaller veterans could train.

name: Code of Hermes
description: The Order's law, whose limitations Confluensis agents must observe closely.

name: St. Giles
description: Saint whose statue in Cotentin is used as a fertility charm and allegedly regrows shaved wood.

name: Statue of St. Giles
description: Phallic statue in Cotentin from which healing wood shavings are taken and which reputedly regrows them.

name: Fengheld
description: Covenant in the Rhine Tribunal with chapter houses, including one near Cherbourg; likely to face a crisis.

name: Chapter of Cherbourg
description: Chapter house of Fengheld near Cherbourg, occupied by a single magus considered a cenobite in Normandy.

name: Cherbourg
description: Norman town near which Fengheld founded a chapter house.

name: Chapter House
description: Satellite covenant of a parent covenant; not recognized under Normandy's Peripheral Code.

name: Peripheral Code
description: Local Tribunal rulings supplementing the Code of Hermes.

name: Cenobite
description: A magus living in an unrecognized covenant, as the Cherbourg magus is treated.

name: Proctor
description: Senior Quaesitor leading Confluensis, whose agents the player characters may be.

name: House Guernicus
description: House of the Quaesitores, which would replace Proctor with a senior Quaesitor.

name: Julius Caesar
description: Roman general who concluded his Gallic campaign in 51 BC.

name: St. Denis
description: Saint who evangelized Paris and was martyred at Montmartre in 275.

name: Paris
description: Capital city of France, established by Clovis and Hugh Capet; site of Eboris and the University.

name: Montmartre
description: Hill near Paris where St. Denis was martyred.

name: St. Martin of Tours
description: Saint who gave half his cloak to a beggar and became bishop of Tours.

name: Tours
description: City whose bishops included St. Martin and Gregory; site of the Battle of Tours in 732.

name: St. Perpetuus
description: Bishop of Tours after St. Martin in 397.

name: Huns
description: Invaders of Europe under Attila, defeated at Châlons in 451.

name: Attila
description: Leader of the Huns whose westward conquests ended at Châlons.

name: Merovech
description: Legendary king of the Salian Franks (447-458), ancestor of the Merovingians.

name: Salian Franks
description: Frankish people ruled by Merovech and Childeric.

name: St. Geneviève
description: Saint who saved Paris from the Huns and from Childeric's siege.

name: Battle of Châlons
description: 451 battle in which Romans, Franks and Visigoths defeated the Huns.

name: Childeric
description: Son of Merovech, king of the Salian Franks who besieged Paris in 464.

name: Euric
description: Visigoth king campaigning across Western Europe 470-485.

name: Odovacar
description: Gothic king who conquered Italy in 476.

name: Clovis
description: King of the Franks, founder of the Merovingian dynasty, first Christian Frankish king; his magical lineage endures.

name: Merovingian Dynasty
description: Frankish royal dynasty begun by Clovis, ending with Childeric III.

name: Childebert I
description: Son and successor of Clovis who died childless in 558.

name: Chlotar
description: Brother of Childebert who inherited the Frankish kingship.

name: Sigebert
description: Frankish king who warred on Chilperic in 567.

name: Chilperic I
description: Son of Chlotar, king who died in 584.

name: Fredegund
description: Wife of Chilperic I and regent for Chlotar II.

name: Chlotar II
description: Chlotar 'the Grand', reunited the Frankish kingdom in 613.

name: St. Gregory of Tours
description: Bishop of Tours who wrote the Historia Francorum.

name: Historia Francorum
description: History of the Franks written by St. Gregory of Tours in 594.

name: Dagobert I
description: King of Austrasia and the Franks from 628 to 637.

name: Theoderic III
description: Frankish king under whom the kingdom reunited in 679.

name: Ebroin
description: Mayor of the Palace dominating Theoderic III.

name: Pepin II
description: Pepin 'the Large', Dux et Princeps Francorum.

name: Trianoma
description: Traveled widely 731-767 contacting wizards who visited Bonisagus and became Founders.

name: Bonisagus
description: Founder of the Order of Hermes who swore the Oath in 767.

name: Founders
description: The original magi who founded the Order of Hermes.

name: Battle of Tours
description: 732 victory by Charles Martel over an Islamic army.

name: Charles Martel
description: Son of Pepin II who won the Battle of Tours.

name: Pepin III
description: Pepin 'the Short', first Carolingian king, crowned 751.

name: Carolingian Dynasty
description: Frankish royal dynasty begun by Pepin III.

name: Childeric III
description: Last Merovingian king, shorn and retired to a monastery.

name: Charlemagne
description: King of the Franks and emperor crowned in 800, who outlawed sorcery but permitted benevolent magic.

name: Oath of Hermes
description: Oath sworn by the Founders in 767.

name: Durenmar
description: Site of the first Tribunal gathering of the Order.

name: Jerbiton
description: Founder who met Charlemagne in 789 and adopted apprentices of Carolinus.

name: Carolinus
description: Charlemagne's mage-smith.

name: Branugurix
description: Domus magna of House Diedne in Brittany, founded 791 and destroyed in 1012.

name: House Diedne
description: Hermetic House destroyed in the Schism War.

name: Tytalus
description: Founder of House Tytalus who stole Hariste and founded Fudarus, vanishing into the Maddenhofen Woods in 807.

name: Hariste
description: Apprentice stolen from Pralix; first Prima of Tytalus.

name: Pralix
description: Magus from whom Tytalus stole Hariste; acting leader of House Tytalus.

name: Maddenhofen Woods
description: Bohemian woods where Tytalus vanished.

name: Bibracte
description: Covenant founded 822, sacked by Montverte in 969.

name: Pagus
description: Covenant founded c.840-855, destroyed 1008.

name: Treaty of Verdun
description: 843 treaty dividing Charlemagne's empire.

name: Baiocassium
description: Covenant founded 851, destroyed 1011.

name: Sinapis
description: Flambeau covenant founded c.855-875, abandoned 1063.

name: Tribunal
description: Regional Hermetic governing gathering, requiring at least twelve magi from four covenants.

name: West Franks Tribunal
description: Tribunal named in 865, predecessor of the Normandy Tribunal.

name: Britannian Tribunal
description: One of the Tribunals named in 865.

name: Roman Tribunal
description: One of the Tribunals named in 865.

name: Theban Tribunal
description: One of the Tribunals named in 865.

name: Eastern Tribunal
description: One of the Tribunals named in 865.

name: Greater Alps Tribunal
description: One of the Tribunals named in 865.

name: Rotomagus
description: Covenant founded c.875, destroyed in 892 when Vikings sacked Rouen.

name: Rouen
description: City sacked by Vikings in 892.

name: Charles the Fat
description: Emperor who reunited Charlemagne's empire in 881, deposed 887.

name: Odo, Count of Paris
description: Chosen king of the Franks in 888 for resisting the Norse.

name: Charles the Simple
description: King of the Franks from 898, driven out by Robert.

name: Florum
description: Covenant founded 907, moved in 1117.

name: Cluny
description: Monastery founded 910.

name: Ligurio
description: Covenant founded 913, destroyed 1011.

name: Kerguntuil
description: Covenant founded 920, destroyed 1007.

name: Robert I
description: Brother of Odo, crowned king in 922, died in combat in 923.

name: Rudolph, Duke of Burgundy
description: Took the Frankish throne in 923.

name: Louis IV
description: King of the Franks from 936.

name: Baiocassium Minor
description: Covenant founded 936, destroyed 1005.

name: Montverte
description: Covenant founded 941 whose magi sacked Bibracte.

name: Lothair
description: King inheriting his father's crown in 954.

name: Betrayal of House Tytalus
description: 961 event at Fudarus in which Prima Tasgillia was executed for diabolism.

name: Tasgillia
description: Prima of House Tytalus executed for diabolism in 961.

name: Kalliste
description: Filia of Tasgillia who replaced her as Prima.

name: Louis V
description: 'The Indolent', king in 986.

name: Hugh Capet
description: King of France from 987, made Paris his capital.

name: Otto III
description: Holy Roman Emperor supporting Hugh Capet.

name: Adalberon of Reims
description: Archbishop supporting Hugh Capet.

name: Robert II
description: 'The Pious', son of Hugh Capet.

name: Aedes Salii
description: Flambeau covenant founded 998, abandoned 1063.

name: Schism War
description: War against House Diedne 1004-1018, ending with the Tempest.

name: Caput Capra
description: Covenant destroyed in 1005.

name: The Tempest
description: Final battle of the Schism War in 1012 destroying Branugurix.

name: Pertheus
description: Magus of House Tytalus who proposed the right of conquest and the Perthean Compact.

name: Hermetic Tourney
description: Tournament redistributing seized vis sources and access to the Tribunal Library.

name: Orchard of Sour Apples
description: Covenant founded 1020, taken over by Confluensis in 1051.

name: Lixivia
description: Covenant founded 1021, disbanded 1124.

name: Perthean Compact
description: Statutes adopted in 1025 defining magi's rights over nearby vis sources.

name: Oleron
description: Covenant founded 1028.

name: Henry I of France
description: King succeeding in 1031.

name: Conrad II
description: German emperor who defeated Odo of Champagne at Bar.

name: Odo of Champagne
description: Defeated by Conrad II in 1037.

name: Vexatores
description: Covenant founded 1048, abandoned 1064.

name: Dragon's Rest
description: Covenant established at the former site of Confluensis in 1051.

name: Philip I
description: 'The Fair', king from 1061.

name: Baldwin V of Flanders
description: Co-regent for Philip I.

name: House Flambeau
description: House whose conflict with Tytalus ended in 1063.

name: Lapis Crudus
description: Joint Tytalus-Flambeau covenant founded 1063, trapped in its regio in 1118, re-emerged 1215.

name: Regio
description: Supernatural layered area in which Lapis Crudus became trapped.

name: Battle of Hastings
description: 1066 battle leading to the Norman conquest of England.

name: William of Normandy
description: Duke who defeated Harold Godwinson at Hastings.

name: Harold Godwinson
description: Anglo-Saxon King of England defeated at Hastings.

name: Nauche-Fleur
description: Covenant founded 1072, abandoned 1166.

name: Perpauca
description: Magus whose books became the first tomes of the Library of the Normandy Tribunal.

name: Library of the Normandy Tribunal
description: Tribunal library begun with Perpauca's books; access given as tourney prizes.

name: Crusades
description: Series of crusades (First through Eighth) from 1096.

name: Cîteaux
description: Monastery founded 1098, mother house of the Cistercian Order.

name: Cistercian Order
description: Monastic order whose mother house is Cîteaux.

name: Infelicitas
description: Covenant founded 1099, abandoned 1158.

name: Nidi
description: Covenant founded 1100.

name: Louis VI
description: 'The Fat', crowned in Orléans in 1108.

name: Reims
description: Traditional coronation city.

name: Picardy
description: Region where a plague of restless dead arose in 1109.

name: Donatores
description: Lineage of House Ex Miscellanea founded by hedge wizards who banished the restless dead of Picardy.

name: House Ex Miscellanea
description: House containing the Donatores lineage.

name: Hedge Wizard
description: Non-Hermetic wizards; some founded the Donatores.

name: Restless Dead
description: Plague of undead in Picardy in 1109.

name: St. Bernard of Clairvaux
description: Founded Clairvaux Abbey and preached the Second Crusade.

name: Clairvaux Abbey
description: Abbey founded by St. Bernard in 1115.

name: Spider's Palace
description: Covenant founded 1117 at the former site of Florum.

name: Peter Abélard
description: Scholar who came to Paris in 1118.

name: Requies Aeterna
description: Covenant founded by Donatores magi in 1123.

name: Alcuin's Auberge
description: Covenant founded 1124, destroyed 1197.

name: Geoffrey V of Anjou
description: Married Matilda, conquered Normandy in 1144.

name: Matilda
description: Daughter of Henry I of England, wife of Geoffrey V.

name: Pope Innocent II
description: Pope who took refuge in France in 1130.

name: Flanders
description: Coast reshaped by a tidal wave in 1134.

name: Bruges
description: City regaining North Sea access in 1134.

name: Moles Magna
description: Covenant founded 1136, destroyed 1182.

name: Louis VII
description: 'The Young', king from 1137, married Eleanor of Aquitaine.

name: Eleanor of Aquitaine
description: Queen who married Louis VII then Henry II; ransomed Richard; died 1204.

name: Normandy
description: Duchy conquered by Geoffrey V and later invaded by Philip II.

name: Henry II of England
description: Henry Plantagenet, begun the Angevin Dynasty in 1154.

name: Angevin Dynasty
description: Royal dynasty beginning with Henry II.

name: Cathedral of Notre-Dame
description: Paris cathedral begun 1163.

name: Philip II Augustus
description: King of France from 1180, built the Louvre, won at Bouvines.

name: Atsingani
description: Covenant founded 1187.

name: Richard the Lionheart
description: King of England who defeated Philip II several times; slain 1199.

name: Louvre
description: Philip II's fortress in Paris.

name: King John of England
description: Richard's brother and successor who lost Normandy.

name: Chartres
description: City with a cathedral damaged by the Great Fire of 1194.

name: University of Paris
description: University chartered by Philip II in 1200.

name: Atramentum
description: Covenant founded 1200, disbanded and reformed as Atramentum Renatus.

name: Exspectatio
description: Covenant founded 1201 on the site of Atramentum.

name: Atramentum Renatus
description: Reformation of Atramentum in 1201.

name: Arthur of Brittany
description: Claimant supported by Philip II against John.

name: Capetians
description: French royal dynasty contending with the Angevins.

name: Eboris
description: Covenant founded in Paris in 1204.

name: Children's Crusade
description: 1212 crusade started by a shepherd boy from Châteaudun.

name: Battle of Bouvines
description: 1214 victory of Philip II over Saxons, English and Flemish.

name: Frederick II
description: German emperor, Holy Roman Emperor from 1220.

name: Louis VIII
description: King of France from 1223.

name: Louis IX
description: King from 1226, canonized as St. Louis.

name: Pope Urban IV
description: Jacques Pantaléon from Troyes.

name: Pope Clement IV
description: Guido Le Gros from Saint-Gilles.

name: Pope Martin IV
description: Simon de Brie.

name: Philip IV
description: 'The Fair', king from 1285.

name: French
description: Living Language of most of the Tribunal (Langues d'Oil), with dialects Orleanais, Norman, Picard, Walloon, Champenois, Bourguignon, Lorrain, Poitevin.

name: Occitan
description: Living Language (Langues d'Oc) with dialects Gascon, Limousin, Auvergnat, Provencal, Catalan.

name: Breton
description: Living Language of Brittany, related to Cornish and Welsh, hardly ever written.

name: Low German
description: Living Language with Frisian and Flemish dialects.

name: Anglo-Norman
description: Dialect of England's ruling classes closely related to Norman French.

name: Latin
description: Language of learning in which most books are written.

name: Living Language
description: Ability category for spoken languages, with dialect specialties.

name: Ile de France
description: Region including Paris, where Orleanais is spoken.

name: Channel Islands
description: Islands where a dialect close to Norman is spoken.

name: Aquitaine
description: Region divided between Poitevin French and Occitan speakers.

name: Anjou
description: County whose dialect is Poitevin; claimed by Philip II.

name: Champagne
description: Region where Champenois is spoken.

name: Burgundy
description: Region where Bourguignon is spoken.

name: Upper Lorraine
description: Region where Lorrain is spoken.

name: Lower Lorraine
description: Region where Walloon is spoken.
